display.purpose: Page and section headings at 28px, weight 600, tracking 0.05em, line-height 1.1. Uppercase with balanced wrapping — the engraved editorial voice.

title.purpose: Card, Dialog and header titles at 20px, weight 600, tracking 0.05em, line-height 1.15. Uppercase with balanced wrapping — the workhorse structural voice.

label.purpose: Buttons, field labels, nav links, command headings and shortcuts. Uppercase 12px caps at weight 600, tracking 0.08em (0.96px), line-height 1.

body.purpose: Default copy and card content at 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.5 with text-wrap: pretty. Weight 500 is the light-on-dark compensation on the forest canvas and hide-brown cards, one whole step above caption.

caption.purpose: Descriptions and hints at 14px, weight 400, line-height 1.5 with text-wrap: pretty — copy, never a caps label.

data.purpose: Quantities, counts and prices at 16px, weight 400, line-height 1.3. Tabular figures so columns of digits align; no Penpot equivalent for the numeric variant.

input.purpose: Form controls only, owned by Input and Textarea. 16px, weight 500, line-height 1.5 — one size at every breakpoint; the old md:0.875rem step is gone.

shadows.name: surface-confirmation
shadows.purpose: Tier-2 cards: confirms the tonal lift above the canvas without drawing the edge. Paired with ring-1 ring-border/60.

shadows.name: floating-confirmation
shadows.purpose: Tier-3 modals, popovers and the command palette. Paired with a full-strength ring-1 ring-border.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default for color, background and border transitions on controls (Tailwind transition-all / transition-colors).

motion.name: layer-transition
motion.purpose: Dialog and popover open/close: fade plus a 95% zoom-in, on animate-in / animate-out.

motion.name: press-nudge
motion.purpose: Button active state. The only physical movement in the system.

narrative.overview:
Sklad is the working tool of a small atelier that builds physical goods by hand and runs the whole business itself. The visual world answers to that room: deep forest green as the page floor, warm hide and charcoal as the surfaces, muted brass as the only thing that shines. It is the disciplined serenity of a leather artisan's workshop translated into an interface — organic warmth and natural shelter, never cold tech-noir, never neon, never a glowing dashboard.

The system is quiet by construction. Because recording a material receipt or a batch is a break in the work rather than a sitting-down task, the UI recedes: one content column, no ornament, no color competing with the data. What carries the identity is not decoration but geometry and material — a single sans face set in uppercase editorial caps, sharp unrounded corners on every shipped element, and depth built from tonal surface steps rather than floating cards. Hierarchy comes from type weight and from how light a surface is, not from borders drawn in a second color.

Reliability here is visual: numbers, counts and costs must be readable at a glance on a phone at the bench, and a destructive action must never be mistaken for an ordinary one. Every rule below exists to keep that reading honest.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only presentation; the light block in `tailwind.css` is documentation, not a shipped mode.
One typeface (Manrope) in an uppercase-caps editorial hierarchy, at a 1rem reading floor with a 65ch prose measure.
Brass is rare and always carries Deep Forest text; brown is a surface, never an accent.
`rounded-none` on every shipped component — sharp sera geometry.
Depth by tonal layering plus hairline `--border` rings; shadows only as a whisper (`shadow-sm`, `shadow-md`).
Single-column `max-w-4xl` shell with a 4px spacing rhythm.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Muted Brass is spent on at most one important thing per view. It always carries Deep Forest text; Warm Off-White on brass is 2.04:1 and must never be used.

rules.name: The Brown Is A Surface Rule
rules.body: Warm Brown fills big surfaces only. It is never an accent, never a small control, and never text on the dark canvas.

rules.name: The No Raw Palette Rule
rules.body: Components reach for semantic tokens. Raw Tailwind palette colors (`text-green-600`, `bg-amber-500`) are off-system, in components and in Penpot alike.

rules.name: The Error Is Ember Rule
rules.body: Destruction and error are Ember: `--invalid` for the underline and the error tint; `--destructive` (Ember fill, Deep Forest label) on the button that acts. Never Warm Off-White on Ember (3.00:1), never Ember as a surface, and never two Ember moments in one view.

rules.name: The Floor-Only Olive Rule
rules.body: Deep Olive is tuned against Deep Forest and stays there. On a brown surface olive linework is a whisper and an olive control is invisible — lift the surface or change the pattern, never darken the token.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: `--muted-foreground` on `--background`, `--muted` and `--card` is the secondary-text pairing and stays ≥ 4.5:1 (4.60:1 on brown) whenever the neutral ramp is touched. Never communicate status by color alone.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Manrope everywhere — copy, controls, headings and labels (`--font-heading` aliases `--font-sans`). No serif, no second display face, no designed mono. Geometry is expressed through caps headings and editorial spacing.

rules.name: The Token-Or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: Never set type with raw utilities (`text-xs`, `text-sm`, `font-*`, `leading-*`, `tracking-*`) in project components. Go through `Typography`. Replace, don't layer: Tailwind emits raw size utilities _after_ the `type-*` utilities, so a leftover `text-sm` wins the cascade — and `cn()` will not resolve the collision. The scale is exposed as `@utility type-*`, not as `--text-*` theme keys, because `cn()` classifies unknown `text-*` strings as colors.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never spans the shell. Copy caps at `--measure-prose` (65ch) and is applied in the prose slots — `CardDescription`, `DialogDescription`, `FieldDescription`, `CommandEmpty` — never on `type-body` itself: the role also covers full-width controls (`InputGroupText`, the command search field), which must keep their box. At the 1rem floor the `max-w-4xl` shell would otherwise run copy to ~109 characters per line; 65ch resolves to ~650px (Manrope's zero advance at 16px is 10px), which lands Cyrillic copy at ~75–79 characters per line.

rules.name: The Wrapping Rule
rules.body: Caps headings (`type-display`, `type-title`) carry `text-wrap: balance` so a two- or three-line title breaks evenly instead of orphaning a word; reading copy (`type-body`, `type-caption`) carries `text-wrap: pretty`, which stops Russian's short prepositions and conjunctions from stranding at a line end. Where the property is unsupported the declaration is simply dropped — no fallback is needed.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Content lives in one `max-w-4xl` column. New surfaces inherit the shell instead of introducing a second grid.

rules.name: The Layer-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: To lift content, move one surface level up the tonal ladder (canvas → Surface 1 → Surface 2 → Surface 3) and add the matching `border` ring. Only then add `shadow-sm` / `shadow-md`, and never invent a third shadow value.

rules.name: The Sharp Sera Rule
rules.body: `rounded-none` is the default and the shipped answer. If a component wants a radius, that is a system-level decision recorded here first — not a local `rounded-lg`.

dos: Do reach for `Button variant="outline"` for the app's default secondary action, and `variant="default"` (brass) for the one primary CTA on a view.
Do keep destructive/confirm actions visually distinct with `variant="destructive"`, and pair destructive intent with a Dialog confirmation.
Do put Deep Forest text on brass — `--primary-foreground` every time.
Do use `gap-*` stacks and the `max-w-4xl` shell for new surfaces.
Do keep `--muted-foreground` for secondary text and `--foreground` for body.
Do lift surfaces tonally (next surface level) before reaching for a shadow.
Do set all type through `Typography` / the `type-*` tokens.
Do use tabular figures (`type-data`) for any column of numbers.
Do verify the `--muted-foreground` pairing stays ≥ 4.5:1 when the neutral ramp changes.
Do chart with the main color palette: `--chart-1` for a single series, deeper steps in order for up to three, and direct labels past that.
donts: Don't put `--foreground` (Warm Off-White) text on `--primary`; it is 2.04:1.
Don't use Warm Brown as an accent, a small control, or as text on the dark canvas.
Don't add radius, colors, fonts or shadow values outside the token set above.
Don't override a component's colors via `className`.
Don't introduce serif, mono or additional display faces, and don't use `font-mono` in project components.
Don't bypass semantic tokens with raw palette colors (`text-green-600` etc.).
Don't communicate status or error by color alone — pair it with a message or icon.
Don't style Penpot text with a typography asset or an off-scale face — bind a `typography.*` token.
Don't maintain or introduce a light theme unless the product requirements explicitly change.
Don't separate chart series with a second hue or with Ember — the main color palette is a tonal ladder of one hue; label the series or vary the line dash.

Don't put olive linework or an olive control on a brown surface, and don't render error as a coloured ink — the `ember.10` tint plus light text is the only recipe, with `--invalid` left to the underline.
Don't put a corner ✕ on a dialog — dismissal is the footer's ghost `Закрыть`, which `DialogFooter` renders for every dialog (upstream shadcn's ✕ is removed on purpose).
